newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban rule out role for ousted leaders.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban rule out role for ousted leaders.

text.p: Afghanistan's new rulers in Kabul, the Taleban, said on Sunday they would soon set up a government to run the country according to Islam but ruled out any role for the ousted leadership.

State-run Radio Pakistan quoted Mullah Mohammad Rabbani, head of a new governing council, as ruling out any role for ousted President Burhanuddin Rabbani, Prime Minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar and their top military commander Ahmad Shah Masood.
"These people are not acceptable to the nation," he was quoted as saying in an interview.
After taking the capital on Friday, the Islamic militia has paused in its pursuit of forces loyal to the ousted president, who were apparently regrouping in the Panjshir Valley north of the city.
Instead it concentrated on consolidating its hold over the capital where it has imposed strict fundamentalist Moslem law.

The U.N. has expressed "grave concern" about the military confrontation, called for an immediate end to fighting and asked all Afghan leaders "to renounce the use of force, to put aside their differences and to engage in a political dialogue."
Mullah Rabbani, no relation of the ousted president, said talks would be held with northern warlord General Abdul Rashid Dostum and all matters with him would be settled through negotiations.
U.N. special envoy Norbert Holl said on Sunday the United Nations wanted to pursue dialogue with the Taleban movement.

"My main message was an offer that the United Nations wants to continue the political dialogue and cooperation with Taleban," he told a news conference after meeting Taleban's Rabbani and the governing council at the presidential palace.
